children: on Tuesday said it delivered two prototype infantry fighting vehicles to the U.S. Army as the service evaluates new capabilities for its armored formations.
The company developed the AMPV 30 vehicles using $17 million of internal research and development funding. The prototypes are based on BAE Systems’ Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicle chassis.
The vehicles were delivered in April for the Army’s Transformation in Contact 2.0 initiative and have since undergone field evaluations, including live-fire testing.
BAE Systems said development of the AMPV 30 took six months from start to delivery.
The vehicles use a common top plate fitted with Kongsberg’s Medium Caliber Turret, a remote turret system that is also in production for the U.S. Marine Corps’ Amphibious Combat Vehicle.

The AMPV 30 prototypes also include counter-drone capabilities, a target handoff system that allows vehicles to share targeting information and a 360-degree camera system designed to provide crews with greater visibility from inside the vehicle.

BAE Systems has been developing the AMPV as a modular platform capable of supporting different weapons and mission systems. The company said its common top plate can accommodate more than 30 turret systems.
The two AMPV 30 vehicles bring BAE Systems’ investment in turreted AMPV prototypes to eight vehicles over the past two years.
The company did not announce a new Army procurement contract or potential contract value associated with the AMPV 30 prototypes.

title: BAE Systems delivers combat vehicle prototypes to U.S. Army
